questions.q: Describe the state of the Indian economy on the eve of Independence.
answer: At Independence in 1947 India inherited a weak, backward and stagnant economy, shaped by nearly two centuries of colonial rule that served British rather than Indian interests.

answer.text: Agriculture, on which most people depended, was stagnant and backward, suffering from oppressive land settlements like the zamindari system, low investment and the forced growing of cash crops for export. Productivity was low and famines were common.

British policy had deindustrialised the country, ruining its famous handicrafts through cheap imports, while modern industry remained small and narrow. India exported raw materials and imported finished goods, and its large export surplus drained wealth to Britain.
Literacy was only about sixteen per cent, life expectancy around thirty-two years, and infrastructure such as railways had been built mainly to serve colonial needs.

answer: Thus India began its independent journey with a fragile and lopsided economy.
